prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a temple standing today that David O. McKay, Spencer W. Kimball or James E. Faust dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where David O. McKay, Spencer W. Kimball, or James E. Faust dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: David O. McKay dedicated Bern Switzerland (1955), London England and Hamilton New Zealand (1958), and Los Angeles and Oakland in the United States. Spencer W. Kimball dedicated Washington D.C. (1974), São Paulo Brazil (1978) and Tokyo Japan (1980). James E. Faust dedicated several temples in 2000, including in Mexico, Costa Rica and the United States.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: McKay: Los Angeles (1956), Oakland (1964). Kimball: Washington D.C. (1974), Seattle (1980), rededications of St. George, Mesa, Laie and Logan. Faust: Medford, Memphis, Nashville, Oklahoma City (2000), Boise rededication (1987).

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Kimball: São Paulo Brazil (1978).

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Faust: Oaxaca Mexico and Tuxtla Gutiérrez Mexico (2000).

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: McKay: London England (1958).

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Kimball: Tokyo Japan (1980).

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: McKay: Hamilton New Zealand (1958).

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: McKay: Bern Switzerland (1955).

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: Faust: San José Costa Rica (2000).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the Americas where a current general officer served as a missionary or mission leader.
prompts.text_original: Several general officers serving as of October 2026 (the Presiding Bishopric and the general presidencies of the Relief Society, Young Women, Primary, Young Men and Sunday School) served as missionaries or mission leaders. Pin a country outside the Americas where one of them served, as named in their official biographies.
prompts.summary: General officers often bring mission experience. As of October 2026, Bishop Waddell had served twice in Spain, Bishop Budge twice in Japan, and Brother Wunderli presided over the Cape Verde Praia Mission. Sister Runia and Brother Reid both served as leaders in Sydney, Australia.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Bishop L. Todd Budge: missionary in the Japan Fukuoka Mission, later president of the Japan Tokyo Mission.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Australia Sydney Mission leaders: Sister Tamara W. Runia (2018 to 2021) and Brother Gabriel W. Reid.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Bishop W. Christopher Waddell: missionary in Spain, later president of the Spain Barcelona Mission.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: Brother Paul V. Johnson: missionary in the Norway Oslo Mission.

answers.name: Cape Verde
answers.fact: Brother David J. Wunderli: president of the Cape Verde Praia Mission, 2020 to 2023.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Spanish- or Portuguese-speaking South American country where lasting missionary work began from 1956 to 1966
prompts.text_original: After the first South American missions in Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay, missionaries pushed west and north. A Spanish- or Portuguese-speaking South American country where lasting full-time missionary work began between 1956 and 1966.
prompts.summary: Missionary work reached Argentina in 1925, Brazil by 1930, Uruguay in 1947 and Paraguay in 1950. Then came a second wave of lasting work: Chile and Peru in 1956, Bolivia in 1964, Ecuador in 1965, and Colombia and Venezuela in 1966.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Parley P. Pratt's 1851-52 mission was brief; Verle M. Allred and Joseph C. Bentley began lasting work in Santiago, June 1956.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: The first full-time missionaries arrived in Lima, August 1956.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: J. Vernon Sharp preached briefly in La Paz in 1927; missionaries arrived to stay in La Paz and Cochabamba, November 1964.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Formal preaching began in Bogota in May 1966, with Spencer W. Kimball present.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: Missionaries from the Andes Mission arrived in Quito, October 1965.

answers.name: Venezuela
answers.fact: Full-time missionaries arrived in Caracas, November 1966.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place named in the Song of Solomon, from Engedi to Lebanon (leave out Tirzah and Kedar)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place named in the Song of Solomon: Lebanon and the tops of Amana, Shenir and Hermon, the tower of Lebanon toward Damascus, Engedi, Carmel and Sharon, Heshbon and Gilead, or Pharaoh's chariots (Tirzah and the tents of Kedar are left out: their sites are not fixed in Church sources)
prompts.note: Mount Hermon (Shenir) sits on the Lebanon-Syria border, so both count. Jerusalem is scored as Israel.
prompts.summary: The Song of Solomon draws its imagery from the whole land: the vineyards of Engedi, the rose of Sharon, the cedars of Lebanon, the heights of Hermon, the pools of Heshbon and the goats of Gilead. It also borrows Pharaoh's chariots (Song 1-7).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Camphire in the vineyards of Engedi, the rose of Sharon, and a head like Carmel (Song 1:14; 2:1; 7:5).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Come with me from Lebanon; the tower of Lebanon looks toward Damascus (Song 4:8; 7:4).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: She is likened to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots (Song 1:9).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Her eyes are like the fishpools in Heshbon, and her hair as a flock of goats from mount Gilead (Song 4:1; 7:4).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: The tower of Lebanon looketh toward Damascus, and the bride is called from the top of Shenir and Hermon (Song 4:8; 7:4).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Jesus or a disciple cast out an evil spirit (not the Gadarene swine or the boy after the Transfiguration)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a town or region where Jesus or one of his disciples, being there, cast out an evil spirit (not the Gadarene swine or the boy healed after the Transfiguration)
prompts.note: Jordan and Syria do not count: the Gadarene site is disputed. Samaria is in the West Bank (Palestine).
prompts.summary: Jesus showed power over evil spirits from his first sermon at Capernaum, and he healed a Gentile girl near Tyre and Sidon. His servants carried the same power: Philip in Samaria, Paul at Philippi, where he freed a slave girl from a spirit of divination, and at Ephesus, where even cloths from him healed.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: In the synagogue at Capernaum Jesus rebuked an unclean spirit, and cast out devils throughout Galilee (Mark 1:21-26, 39).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: At Philippi Paul commanded the spirit of divination to come out of a damsel (Acts 16:16-18).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: In the borders of Tyre and Sidon Jesus cast the devil out of a Syrophenician woman's daughter (Mark 7:24-30).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Philip, one of the seven, preached in the city of Samaria, and unclean spirits came out of many (Acts 6:5; 8:5-7).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: At Ephesus evil spirits went out of the sick through handkerchiefs from Paul (Acts 19:11-12).
